sources.note: Exploratory phase used Constructor Research Platform. Code + predictions public.

items.evidence: Stated design principle: generalization error of the ML-IAP is assumed reduced when the system under study differs from the closest training object by only the coordinates of a single atom, rather than by all atomic positions. Hence the frozen-framework approximation — one mobile ion on a grid, remaining atoms fixed — with grid step <=0.25 A and exclusion of sites within R_min = 1.2 A of other atoms to avoid unphysical configurations. Abstract frames the method as requiring minimal generalization capabilities. Authors contrast this explicitly with active learning, which reduces generalization error but sacrifices the efficiency gained by replacing DFT. Two consequences: (i) hand-crafted Xi outperforms trained multivariate models — logistic regression with L1/L2 and CatBoost on PES descriptors, matminer descriptors, and both combined, none outperform Xi; (ii) the method generalizes to a chemical family absent from tuning data — hydroborates dominate the top of the Xi-ranked list although neither Kahle2020 nor Laskowski2023 contains positively labelled hydroborate electrolytes. Cost: 5997 structures in 7 days on one machine, versus the same time for ML-driven MD on 100 materials; ~50x faster than MLIP-MD, >=3000x than AIMD.
items.caveat: Authors acknowledge the descriptors cannot capture the full complexity of the dynamical effects defining ionic conductivity; the 39% low-conductivity fraction in C1 is the visible cost of the static approximation.
items.flag: novel claim type — about how the field responds to the transferability limit, not about the limit itself. Places maevskiy2025 and nam2025 as opposite strategies: avoid the OOD regime vs. train a surrogate that enters it.

items.evidence: gilmer2017: the message to node v is a sum over neighbours N(v) (Eq. 1); the readout R operates on the set of node states and must be invariant to permutations of those states in order for the MPNN to be invariant to graph isomorphism; Sec. 5.4 shows the tower-mixing step preserves node-permutation invariance; Sec. 3 contrasts Behler-Parrinello representations, described as manifestly isomorphism-invariant, with the Coulomb matrix, where the invariance must instead be learned through dataset augmentation. jacobs2025 names permutations, translation and rotation as the symmetries an atomic environment featurization must respect.
items.caveat: An answer attributing permutation invariance to message-passing aggregation ALONE is incomplete: aggregation carries local ordering, the readout carries global node ordering.

items.evidence: jacobs2025: the local atomic environment is written as a set of densities and expanded in a basis of radial and angular functions (Bessel and spherical harmonics respectively); tensor products over the target atom and its neighbours give values covariant with symmetry operations, and it is common to retain only the scalar-covariant (invariant) features, which can then be used in almost any continuously differentiable ML model. geiger2022 identifies Behler-Parrinello symmetry functions, ACE and SOAP as invariant representations of local atomic environments, and DimeNet as pre-computing triplet angles into scalars.
items.caveat: geiger2022 presents this family as the baseline it argues AGAINST, not as its own mechanism; direction of citation matters. Neither verified source establishes what geometric information is SUFFICIENT - the universality result for distances, angles and dihedrals (GemNet, NeurIPS 2021) is not in this set, so the claim is scoreable at the level of 'this family exists and works this way' only.

items.evidence: geiger2022: all data in the network is typed by how it transforms under the Euclidean group, using irreps of O(3), where l=0 is scalars, l=1 vectors and l=2 the symmetric traceless rank-2 part; Sec. 4.6 defines equivariance and proves that the composition of equivariant functions is equivariant, so constraining each component guarantees whole-network equivariance; spherical harmonics are equivariant with respect to the irrep of matching order (Eq. 6); the tensor product is bilinear and equivariant with selection rules on l and parity (Eq. 16); Eq. 27 states rotation, translation and inversion equivariance together. jacobs2025: recent GNNs such as NequIP, MACE and TeaNet work with highly expressive equivariant tensor representations and operate on them so as to preserve the proper symmetries, and in equivariant networks the additional neighbour attributes are vectors and tensors, giving an atom an environmentally dependent non-spherical character.

items.evidence: gilmer2017 names designing MPNNs that generalize to larger graphs than those in training as an important future direction, and gives two specific reasons why spatial information makes this harder: the pairwise distance distribution depends heavily on the number of atoms, and the most successful use of spatial information creates a fully connected graph in which the number of incoming messages also depends on the number of nodes; it proposes attention over incoming message vectors as a possible remedy. jacobs2025: the true domain of applicability of U-MLIPs is quite uncertain, with areas of major weakness that cannot easily be predicted in advance - a U-MLIP might give excellent diffusivities for 95% of materials and be quite far off for 5%.

sources.note: Accepted 2025-01-13, online 2025-02-26. Keeps mathematics and formalism to a minimum by its own statement: strong for taxonomy, weak for derivations. Used here only where it speaks in its own voice; claims resting on results it merely reports have been removed.

items.evidence: jacobs2025 describes two strategies. First, implicit renormalization of long-range effects into short-range interactions, which works for homogeneous condensed-phase systems with strong screening; it reports Ceder et al.'s analysis that this success rests on local charge neutrality, which correlates with lower-energy states, while higher-energy states with weaker local charge neutrality have electrostatic interactions that are not well represented by short-range terms - so researchers should be very careful about using only short-range interactions for simulations exploring higher-energy states. Second, explicit long-range terms: Coulomb's law via maximally localized Wannier centres (DeepPot, SCFNN), and DFT-D3 vdW plus electrostatic corrections as explicit energy terms (AIMNet2, MACE-MP0, SO3LR). Fig. 8 decomposes total potential energy into local, dispersion, electrostatic and induction contributions.
items.caveat: This is the boundary condition on Q18.C4 and Q18.C5: the locality ansatz is condition-dependent, not universal. An answer stating locality and per-atom decomposition as mechanisms without stating their failure regime is incomplete.

items.evidence: bheemaguli2025: 574 migration paths across layered/Weberite/spinel/olivine/perovskite/NaSICON, Li/Na/Mg/Ca. Classification at 500 meV: Orb-v3 84.84% (487/574), SevenNet 82.93%, MACE-MP-0 79.44%, CHGNet 73.87%, M3GNet 73.52%. But Em MAE 0.310-0.349 eV full set, 0.198-0.257 eV after per-model outlier removal, against a DFT-NEB reference uncertainty of ~60 meV, where 60 meV at 298 K corresponds to an order-of-magnitude change in D. maevskiy2025: 8 of 10 top-ranked structures confirmed superionic at room temperature by AIMD; SevenNet-MD validation gives 55% of top-100 above 0.1 mS/cm vs ~7% (2/29) unbiased — 8-fold enrichment. But 39% of the same Xi-selected set falls below 0.005 mS/cm, which the authors attribute to mechanisms not captured by the FV descriptors.
items.flag: the two sources converge on the same shape of result: reliable ranking, unreliable magnitude

sources.title: Evaluation of Foundational Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials for Migration Barrier Predictions
sources.note: Authors state no prior benchmark of universal potentials for Em existed. Data on GitHub + Zenodo.

items.evidence: Seven equal-size Em bins over 574 paths. Fraction within 0.1 eV in highest bin (~1.31-2.50 eV): Orb-v3 20.7%, MACE-MP-0 18.3%, SevenNet 14.6%, M3GNet 6.1%, CHGNet 3.7%. Lowest bin (~0.0025-0.25 eV): all above 50% (CHGNet 59.8% highest). Compounding directional bias: CHGNet and M3GNet underestimate Em in 73.1% and 78.2% of predictions (420/154 and 449/125 under/over); MACE-MP-0, SevenNet, Orb-v3 balanced (299/275, 244/330, 242/332). Authors frame this as the specialized-vs-generalized trade-off: simpler graph models peak on low Em, complex models sacrifice peak performance for range.
items.flag: distinct from composition and temperature axes; means benchmark-average MAE conceals where the method actually fails

items.evidence: bheemaguli2025: no positive correlation between Em accuracy and local-geometry accuracy, and an inverse relationship — best geometry predictions coincide with worst Em predictions. Bin 5 geometry success 66.7/75.0/66.7/66.7/58.3%; Em success 16.7/0/16.7/8.3/0%. Only two models achieve >0.5 on both metrics, and only in bin 1. sources.title: Flow matching for accelerated simulation of atomic transport in crystalline materials

items.evidence: Below the training temperature range LiFlow D* decreases much more slowly than the fine-tuned-MLIP reference — fictitious diffusion on extrapolation, attributed to training predominantly on larger Li displacements at higher T. Second mode: collapse toward non-diffusive displacements when hopping is rare (gamma-LPS, low T), underestimating D*. Structural features fail in the opposite direction: PMFs accurate at low T, noisier and free-energy-smoothed at high T. Authors state the model lacks the broad generalizability of universal MLIPs.

source.title: Flow matching for accelerated simulation of atomic transport in crystalline materials

candidates.surface_form: A direct regression (Regressor) model yields higher mean‑squared‑displacement errors than the generative LiFlow model, demonstrating the necessity of generative modeling for accurate atomic transport simulation.

Incorporating an adaptive, thermally and chemically conditioned Maxwell–Boltzmann prior markedly lowers mean absolute errors and raises rank correlations for MSD and RDF compared with an isotropic prior; ablation studies show performance degradation without it.
Incorporating the Corrector model reduces RDF mean absolute error and mitigates large‑displacement artifacts, improving MSD prediction across temperatures, especially for hydrogen diffusion.

items.interpretation: Conservative automated alignment proxy; not human-verified scientific truth

items.ground_truth_claim: Demonstrated generality is bounded by the ansatz, not by data volume: structural assumptions exclude whole classes of observable that no additional training removes

sources.title: GNN-assisted phase space integration with application to atomistics

items.evidence: saxena2023: interatomic independence (Sigma_ij = 0), Einstein-solid approximation, quasistatic limit with vanishing mean and thermal momenta; authors state correlations responsible for nonequilibrium irreversible thermal transport must be modelled separately — transport excluded by construction, not merely untested. Contrast case nan2024 (no ML): T_CG = n³·T_AA makes temperature a bookkeeping quantity (11,200 / 37,800 / 89,600 K nominal for a 1400 K target), so transition temperature is not an observable; n³:1 beads carry no charge, so conductivity is not representable; hard ceiling n<=4 at 5% bond-length error.
items.caveat: The generalization across ML and non-ML cases is ours; each source states only its own constraint.
items.flag: distinguishes ansatz-limited from data-limited failure — a different mechanism from the training-distribution explanations in Q15.C7

sources.title: Predicting ionic conductivity in solids from the machine-learned potential energy landscape
sources.note: Exploratory phase used Constructor Research Platform. Code + predictions public.

items.evidence: Stated design principle: generalization error of the ML-IAP is assumed reduced when the system under study differs from the closest training object by only the coordinates of a single atom, rather than by all atomic positions. Hence the frozen-framework approximation — one mobile ion on a grid, remaining atoms fixed — with grid step <=0.25 A and exclusion of sites within R_min = 1.2 A of other atoms to avoid unphysical configurations. Abstract frames the method as requiring minimal generalization capabilities. Authors contrast this explicitly with active learning, which reduces generalization error but sacrifices the efficiency gained by replacing DFT. Two consequences: (i) hand-crafted Xi outperforms trained multivariate models — logistic regression with L1/L2 and CatBoost on PES descriptors, matminer descriptors, and both combined, none outperform Xi; (ii) the method generalizes to a chemical family absent from tuning data — hydroborates dominate the top of the Xi-ranked list although neither Kahle2020 nor Laskowski2023 contains positively labelled hydroborate electrolytes. Cost: 5997 structures in 7 days on one machine, versus the same time for ML-driven MD on 100 materials; ~50x faster than MLIP-MD, >=3000x than AIMD.
items.caveat: Authors acknowledge the descriptors cannot capture the full complexity of the dynamical effects defining ionic conductivity; the 39% low-conductivity fraction in C1 is the visible cost of the static approximation.
items.flag: novel claim type — about how the field responds to the transferability limit, not about the limit itself. Places maevskiy2025 and nam2025 as opposite strategies: avoid the OOD regime vs. train a surrogate that enters it.

sources.title: A practical guide to machine learning interatomic potentials - Status and future
sources.venue: Curr. Opin. Solid State Mater. Sci. 35:101214
sources.note: Accepted 2025-01-13, online 2025-02-26. Keeps mathematics and formalism to a minimum by its own statement: strong for taxonomy, weak for derivations. Used here only where it speaks in its own voice; claims resting on results it merely reports have been removed.

items.evidence: gilmer2017: the message to node v is a sum over neighbours N(v) (Eq. 1); the readout R operates on the set of node states and must be invariant to permutations of those states in order for the MPNN to be invariant to graph isomorphism; Sec. 5.4 shows the tower-mixing step preserves node-permutation invariance; Sec. 3 contrasts Behler-Parrinello representations, described as manifestly isomorphism-invariant, with the Coulomb matrix, where the invariance must instead be learned through dataset augmentation. jacobs2025 names permutations, translation and rotation as the symmetries an atomic environment featurization must respect.
items.caveat: An answer attributing permutation invariance to message-passing aggregation ALONE is incomplete: aggregation carries local ordering, the readout carries global node ordering.

sources.note: Self-described as a draft. Body text dated January 2021, arXiv posting 2022-07-18; use the posting date for cutoff. Only source in the set that derives the equivariance machinery rather than naming it.

items.evidence: jacobs2025: the local atomic environment is written as a set of densities and expanded in a basis of radial and angular functions (Bessel and spherical harmonics respectively); tensor products over the target atom and its neighbours give values covariant with symmetry operations, and it is common to retain only the scalar-covariant (invariant) features, which can then be used in almost any continuously differentiable ML model. geiger2022 identifies Behler-Parrinello symmetry functions, ACE and SOAP as invariant representations of local atomic environments, and DimeNet as pre-computing triplet angles into scalars.
items.caveat: geiger2022 presents this family as the baseline it argues AGAINST, not as its own mechanism; direction of citation matters. Neither verified source establishes what geometric information is SUFFICIENT - the universality result for distances, angles and dihedrals (GemNet, NeurIPS 2021) is not in this set, so the claim is scoreable at the level of 'this family exists and works this way' only.

items.evidence: geiger2022: all data in the network is typed by how it transforms under the Euclidean group, using irreps of O(3), where l=0 is scalars, l=1 vectors and l=2 the symmetric traceless rank-2 part; Sec. 4.6 defines equivariance and proves that the composition of equivariant functions is equivariant, so constraining each component guarantees whole-network equivariance; spherical harmonics are equivariant with respect to the irrep of matching order (Eq. 6); the tensor product is bilinear and equivariant with selection rules on l and parity (Eq. 16); Eq. 27 states rotation, translation and inversion equivariance together. jacobs2025: recent GNNs such as NequIP, MACE and TeaNet work with highly expressive equivariant tensor representations and operate on them so as to preserve the proper symmetries, and in equivariant networks the additional neighbour attributes are vectors and tensors, giving an atom an environmentally dependent non-spherical character.

sources.title: Learning Inter-Atomic Potentials without Explicit Equivariance (TransIP)
sources.note: NOT read in full. Abstract, conclusion and author list verified. Sufficient for the mechanism-existence claim Q18.C7, where the abstract IS the claim. Do not cite for internal detail beyond the reported 40-60% improvement over a data-augmentation baseline on OMol25.

items.evidence: elhag2025: state-of-the-art models enforce roto-translational symmetries through equivariant architectures, described as a hard-wired inductive bias that can reduce flexibility, computational efficiency and scalability; TransIP instead guides a generic non-equivariant Transformer to learn SO(3)-equivariance by optimizing its representations in the embedding space, attaining performance comparable to equivariant baselines on OMol25 and a 40-60% improvement over a data-augmentation baseline across dataset sizes.
items.caveat: Single-source claim, verified at abstract and conclusion level only. Related mechanisms in the same family (frame averaging, local-frame architectures) are NOT verified and must not be scored.

items.evidence: gilmer2017 names designing MPNNs that generalize to larger graphs than those in training as an important future direction, and gives two specific reasons why spatial information makes this harder: the pairwise distance distribution depends heavily on the number of atoms, and the most successful use of spatial information creates a fully connected graph in which the number of incoming messages also depends on the number of nodes; it proposes attention over incoming message vectors as a possible remedy. jacobs2025: the true domain of applicability of U-MLIPs is quite uncertain, with areas of major weakness that cannot easily be predicted in advance - a U-MLIP might give excellent diffusivities for 95% of materials and be quite far off for 5%.
items.caveat: gilmer2017 is a 2017 molecular-property paper, not an MLIP paper, and its models are permutation-invariant and distance-based yet still fail this transfer - which is precisely why it is load-bearing. It does not test per-atom-energy MLIP architectures.

sources.note: Accepted 2025-01-13, online 2025-02-26. Keeps mathematics and formalism to a minimum by its own statement: strong for taxonomy, weak for derivations. Used here only where it speaks in its own voice; claims resting on results it merely reports have been removed.

items.evidence: jacobs2025 describes two strategies. First, implicit renormalization of long-range effects into short-range interactions, which works for homogeneous condensed-phase systems with strong screening; it reports Ceder et al.'s analysis that this success rests on local charge neutrality, which correlates with lower-energy states, while higher-energy states with weaker local charge neutrality have electrostatic interactions that are not well represented by short-range terms - so researchers should be very careful about using only short-range interactions for simulations exploring higher-energy states. Second, explicit long-range terms: Coulomb's law via maximally localized Wannier centres (DeepPot, SCFNN), and DFT-D3 vdW plus electrostatic corrections as explicit energy terms (AIMNet2, MACE-MP0, SO3LR). Fig. 8 decomposes total potential energy into local, dispersion, electrostatic and induction contributions.
items.caveat: This is the boundary condition on Q18.C4 and Q18.C5: the locality ansatz is condition-dependent, not universal. An answer stating locality and per-atom decomposition as mechanisms without stating their failure regime is incomplete.

items.evidence: sanocki2025: the vastness of chemical space makes generalization a central challenge for MLIPs, whose usefulness is often limited by poor transferability to out-of-distribution samples; a systematic evaluation of MLIP architectures with long-range corrections across diverse chemical spaces finds such schemes essential not only for improving in-distribution performance but, more importantly, for enabling significant gains in transferability to unseen regions of chemical space.
items.caveat: Verified at abstract level only; do not score internal quantitative detail. This is the ONLY claim in the set giving directional evidence that a constraint choice measurably improves out-of-distribution transfer, which is the second half of the question. Its direction is notable: the gain comes from RELAXING locality, not from adding a symmetry constraint.

candidates.surface_form: Long-range correction schemes in machine learning interatomic potentials are essential for achieving state-of-the-art accuracy, improving in-distribution performance, and enabling significant gains in transferability to unseen regions of chemical space.

MACE without long-range correction does not generalize well to out-of-distribution samples, while integration of long-range correction schemes has significant effects on both MACE and Allegro architectures.

Biased train-test splitting strategies including cluster, maximal separation, size, and random splits enable rigorous benchmarking by explicitly testing model performance in significantly different regions of chemical space.
